name: Tod und Leben
description: Tod und Leben (Death and Life) is a simple German card game for two players, similar to War. It is distinct in that players have their own draw piles and must win cards to stay 'alive'. The game ends when one player loses all their cards (Death) and the other has all of them (Life).

overview.description: Tod und Leben (Death and Life) is a simple German card game for two players, similar to War. It is distinct in that players have their own draw piles and must win cards to stay 'alive'. The game ends when one player loses all their cards (Death) and the other has all of them (Life).

history.origins: Tod und Leben is a German folk game in the War family. German War-style variants including Bettelmann (Beggar Man) and Tod und Leben were documented as early as 1833 in C.F. Schenkel's Oekonomische Encyclopaedia (Berlin). The game uses a 32-card Skat pack; one reported variant was played by Günther Senst as a child in Mecklenburg. It has remained a common children's pastime in Germany, with play continuing until one player holds all cards (Life) and the other has none (Death).
timeline: 1833: German War variants including Tod und Leben documented in Schenkel's encyclopedia.
19th century: played in Mecklenburg and elsewhere as a children's game.
history.cultural: Common children's game in Germany; often played with German-suited cards; no strategy, purely luck-based.
history.evolution: Evolved from the broader War family; German 32-card form fixed as a two-player game with recycled or round-based play.

setup.dealing: Deal all cards (16 each) into two face-down piles.

rules.objective: Collect all 32 cards by winning battles: each player reveals the top card of their pile simultaneously; the higher rank takes both cards to the bottom of their pile. On ties, war: each plays one face-down then one face-up; higher face-up wins all. The last player with cards wins (Life); the other loses (Death).
rules.gameplay: Simultaneous reveal of top card. Higher card wins both. Winner puts cards at bottom of their pile. Ties: War mechanism (play one down, one up, compare).
keyRules: Win all cards to win game

strategy.intermediate: No distinct intermediate; game is purely luck-based.
strategy.advanced: No advanced tier; no meaningful strategy beyond accepting outcomes.

variations.name: Round-based
variations.description: Play through all 16 cards once per round; cards are not recycled. Whoever won more cards in the round wins. Game can continue for as many rounds as desired.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Round-based variant differs in play structure; no engine constant overrides identified from source.
